definitions: A technique used in large language models (LLMs) to reduce the memory footprint and computational cost of the key and value (K/V) caches during inference.
The process of converting the floating-point numbers in the K/V cache to lower-precision integers, thereby saving memory and potentially speeding up computations.
examples: Implementing K/V cache quantization can significantly improve the efficiency of LLM deployment.
Researchers are exploring various methods for effective K/V cache quantization.
The benefits of K/V cache quantization are particularly evident in resource-constrained environments.
